newsitem.title: UK: MMC referral clouds B.Gas dividend policy.
newsitem.headline: MMC referral clouds B.Gas dividend policy.

text.p: The referral of the TransCo review to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission means prolonged uncertainty over British Gas' dividend policy, analysts said.

"British Gas has the hope it may salvage something, but there are absolutely no guarantees," said analyst Irene Himona at SG Strauss Turnbull. "This means we will not find out the full story for the dividend for another nine months," she added.
British Gas asked for a referral of the crucial TransCo review after months trying to persuade regulator Ofgas to go easy on TransCo, its pipeline operating unit, failed.
The utility said earlier that Ofgas' proposals would slash TransCo's cash flow by at least 400 million stg per year.
It would, however, not say what this would mean for its dividend policy, but industry watchers reckon the pay-out would have to be trimmed by some 10 percent if Ofgas' proposals were implemented.
The stock market had braced itself for such a dividend cut ever since Ofgas' initial proposals were published early in May and shares slumped 25 percent in the following two weeks.
At the moment, investors would rather accept the price review than face a lengthy MMC enquiry.
British Gas shares fell 5-1/2 pence to 194 after the utility announced it wanted the MMC to vet the price proposals.
The referral is likely to make British Gas put a negative spin on any new developments in an effort to win the MMC's sympathy, said analysts.
"There is no point in telling the MMC that things are going wonderfully if you are going through a regulatory review," said Kleinwort Benson's Paul Spedding.
Instead, it is more likely that British Gas will start a fresh campaign to stress even more the financial damage caused by the proposed price control, he added.
The news of the referral comes on top of investor disappointment that British Gas was unable to agree the sale of part of its loss-making gas supply business to Scottish Hydro-Electric.

The deal promised to give valuable clues on the company's worth ahead of its planned split-up into separate trading and transport arms early next year. The MMC referral has also reduced BG's chances of agreeing any sell-off, analysts said.
"They (British Gas) are going to be heavily focused on the MMC enquiry, so the idea of diverting management's attention to a deal like that is unlikely," said Spedding.

British Gas executives are already under strain as they try to re-negotiate crippling Take-or-Pay contracts, which oblige the utility to buy gas from North Sea producers at prices well above market rates.
The company said earlier this month that the negotiations were intense and that progress was "gradual."
British Gas, privatised 10 years ago, is still struggling hard on many fronts to cope with the loss of its monopoly.
Analysts, however, would have preferred it to accept defeat today in one battle and focus on other challenges.
"Shareholders now don't know where they stand and that is bad news," said Himona.
